clue.text: Fellow's in the dark in Russian port

indicators.note: the fellow's word sits inside the word for darkness, so 'in' here signals one piece placed within another

parts.note: murk is gloom or darkness
a fellow is a man; with the possessive 's it gives MANS

explanation.surface: A man is lost in the gloom of a northern Russian harbour city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow's' reads as a possessive in the surface, but here the 's stays as a letter of the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Murmansk is an ice-free seaport on the Kola Peninsula in Arctic Russia.

clue.text: Associate of Mike sits on cinder

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed above, sitting on top of, the second

parts.note: Mike is the radio alphabet code word for M
an ember is a glowing cinder from a fire

explanation.surface: Someone close to Mike is perched on a lump of cinder.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'sits on' means M comes first, above EMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: A member is one who belongs to a group, an associate of it.

clue.text: Building worker upset about hundred left over

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the letter for a hundred, so about signals enclosure
in a down clue, upset means the worker's word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a tiler is a tradesman who lays tiles on a building
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A roofer, distressed, is left with about a hundred spare tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upset' means turned upside down, so the worker is read from bottom to top before 'about' wraps the hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Relict is an old word for something surviving or remaining from an earlier time.

clue.text: Rough bar put in disarray

indicators.note: things in disarray are jumbled, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A rough pub has been left messy after a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disarray' rearranges BAR + PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrupt or curt manner is brusque and rough in its speech.

clue.text: A bloomer making game prolong

parts.note: snap is a children's card game in which matching cards are called out
to drag on is to prolong or go on too long

explanation.surface: A blunder in a card game draws it out tediously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder or a loaf, but here it is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden plant grown for its flowers.

clue.text: Force Isaac used making part of shopfront

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

indicators.note: the name is used, worked over into a new order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Isaac is forced into putting up a sign above a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is an unusual anagram signal: the name is used, worn into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascia is the signboard above a shop window bearing the shop's name.

clue.text: Poles had adapted plant

indicators.note: something adapted is altered, so the letters of these words are reworked

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Polish people had modified a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges POLES + HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphodel is a lily-like flowering plant, in legend growing in the Elysian fields.

clue.text: Coast road hotel embellished with projection moulding

indicators.note: the moulding is decorated by having the hotel letter put into it

parts.note: a cornice is a projecting ornamental moulding along the top of a wall
Hotel is the radio alphabet code word for H

explanation.surface: A seaside hotel is decorated with a fancy jutting moulding.
explanation.walkthrough: A corniche is typically a cliff road along the Mediterranean coast; 'embellished with' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road cut into a cliff along a coastline.

clue.text: Bet on brisk pace of animal

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up before a hand of poker
a lope is a long easy bounding stride

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on how fast an animal runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down entry places ANTE above LOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a swift deer-like grazing mammal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Abuse of whisky has soldier taking a bit of a turn

parts.note: malt is a malt whisky
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a regular crossword abbreviation for soldiers
taken as written

indicators.note: only a small bit of the word is used, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone drinking whisky with a soldier feels slightly dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' takes T, the first letter of 'turn'.
explanation.definitionFit: To maltreat is to treat someone cruelly, to abuse them.

clue.text: Splutter about scripture's meaning

indicators.note: the word for spluttering goes round the scripture letters, so about signals enclosure

parts.note: to spit is to splutter out saliva or words
RI, religious instruction, is the old British school subject of scripture

explanation.surface: Someone splutters about what a holy text means.
explanation.walkthrough: Religious instruction was the traditional British school subject for scripture lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: The spirit of a law or text is its intended sense, as opposed to the letter.

clue.text: Prank creates leak? Put a plug in it!

indicators.note: the plug goes into it, the leak, so the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: an escape is a leak of gas or fluid
a plug is a piece of publicity, an ad

explanation.surface: A plumber is told to stop up a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a plumber's order, but 'plug' is a piece of publicity and 'in it' points back to the leak.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a reckless adventure or mischievous caper.

clue.text: The little woman having a bottle is happy

parts.note: Jo March is one of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women
a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: The wife cheers up with a bottle in her hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The little woman' looks like a wife, but it is Jo from Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial means jolly and cheerful in good humour.

clue.text: Priest introduced to smoother amphibian

indicators.note: the priest is brought into the smoother, placed inside it

parts.note: a sander is a tool that smooths wood
a lama is a Buddhist priest or monk in Tibet

explanation.surface: A clergyman is presented to someone who smooths things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoother' looks like a comparative adjective but is a tool, and 'Priest' is a Tibetan one.
explanation.definitionFit: A salamander is a lizard-like amphibian with moist skin and a tail.

clue.text: Girl eating soldier's meat? That's a blow!

indicators.note: the girl's name takes the soldier in, so eating signals enclosure

parts.note: Kate is a girl's name
RA, the Royal Artillery, gives soldiers; the 's is a link
a chop is a cut of meat such as lamb or pork

explanation.surface: A girl eats a soldier's dinner and gets hit for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meat' looks like part of the soldier's dinner but is a separate piece after the girl-and-soldier container.
explanation.definitionFit: A karate chop is a sharp strike with the side of the hand.

clue.text: Writer allowed to tuck into salmon

indicators.note: the permitted word is tucked into the fish word, placed inside it

parts.note: a smolt is a young salmon heading for the sea
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to eat a salmon dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' suggests eating, but it signals insertion; the salmon here is a young one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobias Smollett was an 18th-century Scottish novelist who wrote Roderick Random.

clue.text: Plain language written about border flower

indicators.note: the written language goes round the border, so about signals enclosure

parts.note: prose is ordinary language, not verse
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Simple words are set down about a herbaceous border bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' suggests a flower bed in the surface, but it is an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow wild flower of early spring.

clue.text: Supplement, if it included cocaine, would be habit-forming

indicators.note: the answer would become the second word if C were added, so C is missing from it

parts.note: something addictive is habit-forming
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: A dietary supplement laced with cocaine would get users hooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Add C to the answer and you get ADDICTIVE; 'would be' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: An additive is a substance added to food or fuel to improve it.

clue.text: Clear one working during feast at midday

indicators.note: these pieces sit in the middle of the meal, as something happening during it

parts.note: a meal is a feast, a repast
to rid is to clear of something
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Someone clears up while working at a noonday banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' reads as an adjective but is a verb here; 'during' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Meridional comes from Latin meridies, noon, and describes things of the noon hour or the south.

clue.text: Various birds that go underwater

definitions.meaning: an old word for several or sundry
loons and similar waterbirds dive below the surface for fish

explanation.surface: Many kinds of bird swim beneath the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective divers means several; the noun is the plural of the bird name.

clue.text: Spatter gold key under pallet

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces are placed beneath the first

parts.note: a pallet is a straw mattress or makeshift bed
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: Gold paint splashes on a key beneath a straw bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' in a down entry places AU + B beneath BED.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to smear or splash with paint or dirt.

clue.text: Old English kingdom won over Elizabeth's favourite

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed over the second

parts.note: W stands for won in sports tables
Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, was a favourite of Queen Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: An ancient kingdom wins over the queen's favourite courtier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in a down entry places W above ESSEX.
explanation.definitionFit: Wessex was the kingdom of the West Saxons in Anglo-Saxon England.

clue.text: It's clear the naughty child wears a hat

indicators.note: the child wears the hat, so the hat goes round the child

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A mischievous youngster obviously has a hat on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link; the definition is the single adjective 'clear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid water is transparent and unclouded.

clue.text: Army headquarters accepts occupation of Asian island

indicators.note: the headquarters takes in the job word, so it contains it

parts.note: a base is a military headquarters
a line is a line of work, an occupation

explanation.surface: Military HQ takes on the job of occupying an Asian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupation' looks military beside the army, but it means a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Balinese describes the people, culture or language of Bali in Indonesia.

clue.text: Evidence about bull turning strange

indicators.note: the whole built word is turned around, read from right to left
the verb goes round the bull word, so about signals enclosure

parts.note: to evidence a claim is to cite something in support
an ox is a bull or steer

explanation.surface: Proof about a bull's behaviour becomes odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evidence' is a verb here, as in to evidence a claim; 'turning' reverses the whole built word.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic means unusual and foreign, strikingly different.

clue.text: Worm stretches laterally

parts.note: to worm or edge is to move slowly and carefully
ways are stretches of distance, as in a long way

explanation.surface: An earthworm extends itself sideways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worm' looks like the creature, but it is a verb meaning to inch along.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgeways means sideways, with the edge foremost.

clue.text: He bets foolishly in ancient Egypt

definitions.note: short for a city in ancient Egypt, a place name

indicators.note: doing something foolishly is doing it wildly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A man gambles recklessly in the land of the pharaohs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' rearranges HE + BETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a great city of the pharaohs on the Nile, near modern Luxor.

clue.text: Squealer's punch clipping holder

parts.note: a grass is British slang for an informer; the 's is a link
to box is to punch

explanation.surface: An informer gets a punch and a newspaper cutting folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipping holder' suggests press cuttings, but it is the box on a lawnmower that catches cut grass. A grass is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassbox is the container on a mower that collects the cut lawn trimmings.
